supporters.quote: When comparing the MCI with the NCI, we did not observe significant differences in hippocampal volume, but significant changes were found in the FISO and NDI metrics in the left CA1–3 region.
supporters.page: 7 (Section 4.3); group result on page 4 (Section 3.2): 'CSVD-MCI patients consistently showing significantly higher values compared to CSVD-NC and healthy controls, particularly in the left hemisphere subiculum ... and CA1–3 region (0.36 ± 0.10 vs. 0.32 ± 0.07 and 0.31 ± 0.06, F = 6.898, P = 0.001, PFDR = 0.005)'
supporters.note: Li et al. 2025, J Affect Disord 384:12-22 (Chongqing, N=169: 58 CSVD-MCI, 54 CSVD-NCI, 57 HC; cross-sectional). A genuine within-study head-to-head: multi-shell NODDI free-water fraction (FISO) in left CA1-3 separates CSVD-MCI from CSVD without cognitive impairment where FreeSurfer subfield volume does not. Limits: the comparator is a CSVD patient group, not healthy adults; the pairwise MCI-vs-NCI statistics are only in Supplementary Material 2 (the main text gives three-group omnibus F tests); the NDI part is weaker than the ledger implies (left CA1-3 NDI omnibus PFDR = 0.066, did not survive FDR, and NDI was HIGHER in MCI); the MCI group carried heavier white-matter-hyperintensity burden than the NCI group (Fazekas p = 0.027), so the free-water difference may track vascular burden; the authors flag CSF partial-volume contamination of FISO at 2 mm resolution.

supporters.quote: Although no behavioral differences were observed between the EMCI and LMCI groups, differences in neural oscillations were observed. (p.1) ... Post hoc tests yielded significant between-group differences on the Go trials, with the LMCI group showing greater ERS than the EMCI group (p = .002, d = 1.155). (p.4)
supporters.note: Lydon et al. 2022, Behav Brain Res 416:113539 (UT Dallas / UT Southwestern, N=35 amnestic MCI: 18 early, 17 late). Supports only a narrower and different form: task-evoked theta separates early from late amnestic MCI where performance on the SAME Go/NoGo task does not. Two elements of the statement are missing. (1) There is no non-impaired comparator: both groups are MCI, the exact ground on which the ledger's own gate audits rejected P-753, P-781 and P-804 ('no non-impaired comparator'). (2) The insensitive measure is behaviour on the same loaded task, not a static or unloaded measure, so this is a neural-versus-behavioural dissociation, not a loaded-versus-static one. Further limits: the groups were defined by logical-memory delayed recall, which differs by construction (p < .001), so 'no behavioural separation' holds only for cognitive-control measures; the between-group EEG difference is confined to theta ERS on Go trials at one of five electrode clusters (alpha interactions gave no between-group post hoc difference, beta nothing); unadjusted sex imbalance (12F/6M vs 4F/13M, p = .026).

supporters.quote: HEC had greater success with decreased emotional intensity relative to MCI (t = 3.205, p = 0.002). No significant group difference was found for the valence rating difference (Rea - Neg). (p.5) ... Most importantly, MCI showed a smaller LPP difference (Rea - Neg) than HEC in the second (t = −2.125, p = .036), third (t = −1.874, p = .064) and fourth (t = −2.009, p = .048) time windows. (p.6)
supporters.note: Xiao et al. 2022, Behav Brain Res 427:113800 (Shanghai Tongji, 46 aMCI vs 47 healthy elderly). Searched for a static or unloaded measure that fails to separate the groups while the ERP succeeds: there is none. The loaded behavioural measure from the same reappraisal task (arousal down-regulation) DID separate aMCI from controls (p = 0.002), and every static neuropsychological measure except ROCF differed (by construction of the groups). The only non-separating measures are themselves task-evoked or task-derived (valence difference; P100, N1 and P300 showed no group effect; early LPP windows no group difference), which cuts against, not for, the claim that task-evoked electrophysiology is the sensitive channel. The LPP differences are uncorrected and marginal (window 3 p = .064, so the ledger's '1100-5000 ms LPP difference did' overstates it). The review's Section 4.2 pairs the ERP with near-identical Hamilton depression scores, but a depression score is not the corresponding static measure of an emotion-regulation ERP, and HAMD >= 14 was an exclusion criterion. Selection: 26 of 72 recruited aMCI (36%) were excluded for inability to complete the task or abnormal behavioural data.

supporters.quote: There was no significant difference in the execution time of single-task TUG test between the MCI and HC groups (p> 0.05), while a significant difference in the execution time of the dual-task paradigm was observed (T= −2.58, p= 0.012). The DTC was also increased in MCI group (T= −2.55, p= 0.014; Table 3).
supporters.note: Zhang et al. 2025, Behav Brain Res 479:115360 (First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou; 30 MCI vs 30 HC; ethics [2021] 475-1). The dual-task limb is supported: single-task Timed Up and Go does not separate MCI from matched controls, dual-task TUG and dual-task cost do. Limits: the dual-task time includes the time to finish dialling an 11-digit number, so part of the 'loaded' measure is the cognitive task itself, on which MCI would be expected to be slower (dialling accuracy did not differ, 70.0% vs 86.7%, p > 0.05); small single-centre sample. The imaging half does not fit the statement: cortical surface area (a static structural index) DID separate MCI from HC in left superior parietal cortex while thickness did not, which is a static-versus-static contrast. CRITICAL: this is the same 60 participants as P-687 (identical demographic table, identical TUG means, same ethics approval), so P-665 and P-687 are one sample reported twice.

supporters.quote: In the whole-brain TBSS analysis, MetS-MCI group demonstrated 6.02 % (8302/137,832 voxels) and 4.38 % (6045/137,832 voxels) of parcellated WM regions with increased values of MD and λ23 in comparison to MetS-NC group (Fig. 2). ... In both comparisons with MetS-NC group and HC group, MetS-MCI group exhibited decreased FA values in left superior corona radiata (SCR.L), left external capsule (EC.L), and right external capsule (EC.R).
supporters.note: Shao et al. 2026, Behav Brain Res 503:116057 (Tongji Hospital, Wuhan; 36 MetS-MCI, 30 MetS-NC, 38 HC). Searched for a macrostructural volume or static structural index compared head-to-head with the diffusion measures: none is analysed (T1 was acquired but no volumetry is reported). FA, MD, axial and radial diffusivity are all tensor parameters from the same diffusion acquisition, so treating FA (or axial diffusivity) as the 'static' counterpart is not a loaded-versus-static contrast. Even that diffusion-internal contrast does not hold: FA did not appear in the whole-brain TBSS MCI-vs-NC text, but the atlas ROI analysis found FA LOWER in MetS-MCI than MetS-NC in three tracts. The lambda1-vs-lambda23 'eightfold' contrast is inferred from two separate comparisons against healthy controls, not a direct test. The study supports only the sensitivity half (diffusion parameters separate MetS-MCI from MetS-NC), which is not the dissociation the statement asserts. ROI tests appear uncorrected (P < 0.05).

supporters.quote: There was no significant difference in the single task execution time between the MCI and HC groups (MCI: 17.29 ± 2.34 s, HC: 17.60 ± 2.89 s, t = 0.47, p = 0.643). However, a significant difference in the execution time of the dual-task paradigm was observed between the two groups (MCI: 29.23 ± 8.02 s, HC: 24.92 ± 4.42 s, t = −2.58, p = 0.012).
supporters.note: Cheng et al. 2024, Hum Mov Sci 97:103257 (Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou; 30 MCI vs 30 HC; ethics [2021]475-1). Same dual-task dissociation, same limits as P-665 (dual-task time includes dialling). NOT INDEPENDENT of P-665: identical group sizes, sex split (4/26 vs 7/23), age (60.50 ± 6.66 vs 58.13 ± 6.50), BMI, education, MoCA medians and TUG values, same department and ethics approval; it is one sample reported in two papers, and the review's own Section 4.2 cites only P-665 (twice). On the macrostructural side this paper runs against the broader framing: whole grey-matter volume (p = 0.038), parenchymal volume (p = 0.039) and right cerebellar anterior-lobe GMV did separate MCI from HC.

narrowed_wording: Not a convergence (two independent samples only). What the sources do support: in two independent single-centre samples a loaded measure separated MCI from a matched comparator where the corresponding static measure did not, hippocampal CA1-3 free-water fraction versus subfield volume in small-vessel-disease MCI versus small-vessel disease without impairment (P-651), and dual-task versus single-task Timed Up and Go in MCI versus healthy controls (one Guangzhou sample, reported in both P-665 and P-687). No supporter shows task-evoked electrophysiology separating MCI from a non-impaired comparator where a static measure fails.
reasoning: Read against the sources, the six supporters reduce to two independent samples. Three papers answer yes (P-651, P-665, P-687), but P-665 and P-687 report the same 60 participants and the same TUG comparison (identical demographics, identical values, same ethics approval), so the dual-task dissociation is one result counted twice. That leaves two independent studies and two method families (NODDI diffusion; dual-task gait), below the three independent studies a convergence requires. The literal count of three yes answers is reached only by that double count. The electrophysiology limb has no supporter that sustains the statement: P-661 compares early with late amnestic MCI (no non-impaired comparator, the ledger's own rejection ground for P-753, P-781 and P-804), and its insensitive measure is behaviour on the same loaded task, not a static measure; P-662's loaded behavioural measure (arousal reappraisal) also separated the groups, several of its task-evoked components did not, and there is no static measure that fails while the ERP succeeds. P-666 contains no macrostructural or static comparator at all (all its measures are diffusion-tensor parameters), and its ROI analysis found FA also lower in MetS-MCI, so it supports only the sensitivity half. The record's claims of five method families and five dataset families, 'each supplying its own within-study head-to-head between the discriminating and the non-discriminating measure', are therefore not borne out: the within-study loaded-versus-static head-to-head exists in P-651 and in the single Guangzhou sample only. Even there the evidence is modest (P-651's pairwise statistics are in the supplement and the MCI arm carried more white-matter-hyperintensity burden; the dual-task time includes the dialling task itself). The statement as the review states it, spanning diffusion microstructure, task-evoked electrophysiology and dual-task performance, fails.
